review: No prior attempt; my own plan from blocks 53-56, 60, 76 and 77. (a) The task's premise fails: eps anticommutes with H, so the positive-energy rest states at the zero, e^{i pi n.x}(1+eps)u, lie on the eps=+1 sublattice. A massive walker at rest has e_x = m w|chi_x|^2 >= 0 there and 0 on the other sublattice, not an alternating density. Any positive-energy eigenstate has e_x = E|psi_x|^2 >= 0; only the mass part alternates, with odd weight (E-m)/(2E), 1/5 at k = pi/2 and m = 3/4 (exact on the 4^3 torus, Gaussian rationals). (b) On a torus the mean-removed rest source is exactly (m/V) eps, and the simplest member's field is exactly u = -(gamma m/(12V)) eps, a pure chessboard of clocks that costs bond energy. Odd-step operators do not feel it (block 76 T1), but a massive walker does: phi(m eps)phi = m e^{u_s}(sinh u_c + eps cosh u_c), a scalar potential plus a mass factor. (c) The HIT condition fails. Both weak-field operators are invertible at pi(111) (symbols 2 and 12), so a Fourier split shows the pull between bodies at rest depends, to every power of 1/R, only on the sources' moments; the staggered part gives terms decaying faster than any power. The 1/R term is -(gamma/4pi)Q_A Q_B/R, the same in both members. A 48^3 illustration shows no 1/R term from a staggered charge. One session, claude-opus-5-5.
